title: The VLOOKUP function: vertical lookup
summary: VLOOKUP looks for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from the column you choose, in the same row.
intro: `VLOOKUP` looks for a value, such as a product code, in the first column of a table, then returns a value from the same row in the column you give by its number. Use `FALSE` for an exact match and `TRUE` to look up sorted bands.
args: The table; its first column is the one searched.
The number of the column to return from, counted from the start of the table.
`FALSE` for an exact match, `TRUE` (the default) for an approximate match.
examples: The price of the product with code `P-102`.
The product name from the second column.
errors: The value is not in the first column, or it has an extra space.
The column number is larger than the number of columns in the table.

faq.a: No, it searches only the first column of the range. To search another column, use `XLOOKUP` or `INDEX` with `MATCH`.

faq.q: How do I hide the `#N/A` error?
faq.a: Wrap the formula in `IFERROR`, such as `=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(...),"Not found")`.
